output.entity_proposed: Refugees and Stateless Persons Protection Board (Protection Board)
output.proposal: HB No. 11736 seeks to protect the rights of refugees and stateless persons by setting out their rights and obligations and the procedures for determining their status, and to create the Refugees and Stateless Persons Protection Board as the central authority on status determination and eligibility for protection, absorbing the related functions of the Bureau of Immigration and the Refugees and Stateless Persons Protection Unit (RSPPU) of the Department of Justice (DOJ).
output.alignment: As a government organization and mandates measure, the review should examine how the Protection Board created under Section 9 (Refugees and Stateless Persons Protection Board) fits with existing bodies, given that the measure transfers the status determination function of the Bureau of Immigration to the Board and abolishes the RSPPU in the DOJ Legal Staff, and whether the creation of a collegial board with four presidential appointees under Section 10 (Composition of the Protection Board) is consistent with the government's intent to streamline agencies and reduce overlapping functions under the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231). The review should also examine the Board's relationship with the DOJ, the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) and the Task Force on Refugee Assistance and Administration. No direct match with the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework priority areas or the LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda was identified.
legislative_history: HB No. 11736 was filed on October 14, 2026 by Representative Patrick Michael "PM" D. Vargas; it is pending at the filing stage, and later stages are not reflected in the available records.
SB No. 616 (20th Congress), filed on July 15, 2025 and pending in the committee, bears the same long title and appears to be the Senate counterpart.

Measures bearing the same or nearly the same title were filed in earlier Congresses: HB No. 3425 and SB No. 379 (18th Congress), and HB No. 4561 and SB No. 2548 (19th Congress), all pending in the committee.

House measures proposing a Refugees and Stateless Persons Protection Office instead of a Board were filed as HB Nos. 10799 and 11265 (19th Congress) and HB Nos. 2339 and 4246 (20th Congress), all pending in the committee.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 11736 seeks to establish a legal framework for the protection of refugees and stateless persons and to create the Refugees and Stateless Persons Protection Board. Its salient features are as follows:
a. Section 9 (Refugees and Stateless Persons Protection Board) provides for the creation of the Protection Board as the central authority on the determination of refugee and stateless status and eligibility for protection, transfers the related responsibility of the Bureau of Immigration to the Board, and abolishes the RSPPU in the DOJ Legal Staff, whose duties the Board shall assume.
b. Section 10 (Composition of the Protection Board) provides that the Board shall be chaired ex officio by the DOJ Secretary, with the DFA Secretary as ex officio Vice Chair, the Commissioner of Immigration and the National Security Adviser as ex officio members, and four members appointed by the President for a non-renewable five-year term, including a civil society representative and three lawyers with at least the qualifications of a regional trial court judge.
c. Section 11 (Powers and Functions of the Protection Board) provides that the Board shall issue rules, decide applications for refugee or stateless status and requests for provisional measures, supervise its Secretariat, promote protection programs, coordinate with the UNHCR and report to competent UN organs.
d. Section 13 (Secretariat) provides that the Board shall be assisted by a Secretariat, which may be drawn from the existing personnel of the RSPPU.
e. Section 29 (Provisional Measures) provides that applicants may be granted provisional measures to protect their personal security, liberty and property pending decision, without prejudice to the issuance of identity papers and travel documents under existing executive issuances.
f. Section 32 (Persons Excluded from the 1951 Refugee Convention and the 1954 UN Convention) provides that the benefits of the Act shall not apply to persons excluded under the two conventions, including those with serious reasons to be considered to have committed war crimes, crimes against humanity or acts of terrorism.
g. The measure further provides for the rights and obligations of refugees and stateless persons, the procedures for applications, interviews, decisions, reconsideration and judicial review, the cancellation, revocation and cessation of status, and an operating budget under Section 14 (Operating Budget).
output.related_measures_policy: HB No. 11736 may be considered alongside SB No. 616, which bears the same title in the Senate, the measures of the same title filed in the 18th and 19th Congresses, and HB Nos. 2339 and 4246, which propose a Refugees and Stateless Persons Protection Office instead of a collegial board. No direct alignment with the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework priority areas or the LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda was identified. The review should assess the transfer of functions from the Bureau of Immigration under Section 9 (Refugees and Stateless Persons Protection Board) in relation to CA No. 613 and EO No. 292, the abolition of the RSPPU and the staffing of the Secretariat under Section 13 (Secretariat), the cost of the four appointive members under Section 10 (Composition of the Protection Board), the source and level of funding under Section 14 (Operating Budget), and the possible overlap with the protection services institutionalized under EO No. 163 (2022).

reviewer_checks: Verify the amount and funding source under Section 14 (Operating Budget), and whether the appointive members are full-time and compensated.

Clarify in Section 10 (Composition of the Protection Board) whether the civil society representative may also be one of the three lawyer appointees, and whether the terms of the appointees should be staggered.
Correct the typographical errors in Section 11 (Powers and Functions of the Protection Board) and Section 29 (Provisional Measures).
Confirm that the reference to RA No. 9372 in Section 32 remains current.

Confirm the status and text of SB No. 616 with the Senate and compare it with this bill.
